title: Securities Trading Policy (Updated August 2023)

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: All directors of the Company (whether executive or otherwise); all members of the boards of subsidiaries; the Managing Director; all other executives reporting to the Managing Director; other executives determined by the Board; and (without limiting the foregoing) all other key management personnel as defined in AASB 124.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Subset of Key Management Personnel distinguished for the clearance contact point (Chairman, or Company Secretary if the Chairman is unavailable or is dealing) and for ASX Appendix 3X/3Y/3Z director's interest notice obligations under Listing Rules 3.19A/3.19B.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Nominees, agents or other associates such as family members, family trusts and family companies of Key Management Personnel; a Director must ensure an Associate does not deal in circumstances that could be attributed to the Director.

definitions.hedging_definition: entering into transactions in associated products which operate to limit the economic risk of security holdings in the Company

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to release to the ASX of the Company's Annual Report
windows.end_anchor: 48 hours after release to the ASX of the Company's Annual Report

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to release to the ASX of the Company's Half Year Report
windows.end_anchor: 48 hours after release to the ASX of the Company's Half Year Report

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to release to the ASX of the Company's Quarterly Reports
windows.end_anchor: 48 hours after release to the ASX of the Company's Quarterly Reports

windows.start_anchor: existence of undisclosed price sensitive information withheld under an ASX Listing Rule exception
windows.end_anchor: beginning of the next trading day after that information is released to the market

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may, from time to time, impose an additional 'ad hoc' prohibition on trading of Securities as a Closed Period. The policy does not state whether such a prohibition is kept confidential.

rules.detail: 'Securities' is defined to include options, warrants, futures or other derivative financial products issued over or in respect of the Company's shares, with no venue restriction, so an OTC purchased put or written call is expressly within the general dealing regime: prior notification to the Chairman/Managing Director (or Company Secretary) that there is no impediment, and avoidance of Closed Periods.
rules.evidence: options, warrants, futures or other derivative financial products issued over or in respect of the Company’s shares or options (Securities).

rules.detail: Hedging (transactions in associated products that limit the economic risk of a security holding) is expressly stated to be subject to the same dealing principles as ordinary trading, i.e. notification and Closed Period restrictions, with no outright ban and no distinction drawn between vested and unvested holdings.
rules.evidence: entering into transactions in associated products which operate to limit the economic risk of security holdings in the Company.

rules.detail: Monetisation structures are not named. 'Deal in Securities' is defined broadly to include entering into transactions in relation to Securities, which would sweep in a prepaid forward or similar monetisation, subjecting it to the same notification and Closed Period requirements as an ordinary sale.
rules.evidence: deal in Securities means buy or sell Securities in the Company, or enter into transactions in relation to Securities in the Company.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named or separately addressed. As a sale of Securities it would fall within the general 'deal in Securities' definition and so require the same prior notification and be barred in Closed Periods, but the policy gives no guidance on borrowing or settlement mechanics.
rules.evidence: deal in Securities means buy or sell Securities in the Company, or enter into transactions in relation to Securities in the Company.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy and is not obviously captured by the 'deal in Securities' definition (buy, sell or enter into transactions in relation to Securities).

CFDs are not named but the policy expressly extends its dealing principles to 'trading in financial products issued or created over the Company's Securities and associated products', which covers a CFD; the same notification and Closed Period regime applies.
rules.evidence: trading in financial products issued or created over the Company’s Securities and associated products.

rules.detail: The policy contains no provision on margin lending, borrowing against Securities, or any financing arrangement.
Granting a charge, lien, mortgage or other security interest over Securities is not mentioned and is not listed within the 'deal in Securities' definition.
No provision addresses secured financing, margin loans or any borrowing secured against Securities of any kind; the policy is silent on financing altogether.

Absolute ban, subject only to a hardship waiver by the Review Officer, on acquiring and disposing of Securities within 6 months of each other; the intervening period is itself treated as a Closed Period.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel must not at any time engage in short-term trading in Securities of the Company. Short-term trading is considered to be trading where the acquisition and disposal of Securities occurs within 6 months of each other.

clearance.approver: Chairman or, in the Chairman's absence, the Company Secretary (Company Secretary if the Chairman is the one dealing)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: immediately on dealing (6.1); details within 2 days (8.1)
clearance.evidence: in the case of Directors the Chairman or, in their absence, the Company Secretary, and notified them of their intention to do so and the Managing Director or Chairman or, in their absence the Company Secretary, indicate that there is no impediment to them doing so.

clearance.approver: Managing Director (Company Secretary if the Managing Director is the one dealing)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: immediately on dealing (6.1); details within 2 days (8.1)
clearance.evidence: they have contacted the Chairman or Managing Director in the case of employees ... and notified them of their intention to do so and the Managing Director or Chairman ... indicate that there is no impediment to them doing so.

clearance.approver: Review Officer (Chairman, or the Board if the Restricted Person dealing is the Chairman)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: immediately on dealing (6.1); details within 2 days (8.1)
clearance.evidence: the Chairman ... (Review Officer) may by issuing prior written clearance to the Key Management Personnel wishing to trade Securities ... waive the requirement of that Restricted Person to deal in Securities outside of the Closed Periods ... Any Written Clearance is valid for a period of 5 trading days following its issue.

carve_outs: Review Officer discretion to permit trading on establishment of hardship
short_term.evidence: Key Management Personnel must not at any time engage in short-term trading in Securities of the Company. Short-term trading is considered to be trading where the acquisition and disposal of Securities occurs within 6 months of each other.

exceptions.approver: Review Officer (Chairman, or the Board if the Restricted Person is the Chairman)
exceptions.evidence: can demonstrate to the Review Officer that the proposed sale or disposal of the relevant Securities is the only reasonable course of action.

the Review Officer may, at their discretion, permit Key Management Personnel to trade in Securities in circumstances that would contravene this paragraph 5.6 if that Key Management Personnel establishes hardship.

the Restricted Person is required by a court order, a court enforceable undertaking ... to transfer or sell securities of the Company or there is some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement to do so.

The prohibition does not apply to acquisitions of shares or options by employees made under employee share or option schemes, nor does it apply to the acquisition of shares as a rule of options under an employee option scheme.

exemption_authority: Review Officer (Chairman, or the Board where the Restricted Person is the Chairman) may grant Written Clearance, valid 5 trading days, to deal during a Closed Period or to override the 6-month short-term trading rule, in cases of severe financial hardship or otherwise exceptional circumstances (paras 5.3-5.7).

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no provision on margin lending, secured financing, encumbrance, or borrowing against Securities of any kind.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike many peer policies, there is no express ban on secured financing, so the loan leg of a funded collar is not itself prohibited by this document; it would only be caught, if at all, as a 'transaction in relation to Securities' requiring the ordinary notification and Closed Period clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The insider trading prohibition extends to dealings by individuals through nominees, agents or other associates, such as family members, family trusts and family companies.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust or controlled company does not escape the notification obligations or Closed Period restrictions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Parties covered by this policy should not procure others to deal during Closed periods.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank counterparty executing hedge trades on the executive's behalf or instruction during a Closed Period could itself be a breach by the executive as 'procuring' a dealing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading is considered to be trading where the acquisition and disposal of Securities occurs within 6 months of each other ... Such a period will be considered a Closed Period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A written call that could result in disposal of the underlying shares within 6 months of vesting (acquisition) would breach the short-term trading ban absent a hardship waiver, so collar tenor and any early-exercise risk should be structured to fall outside that 6-month window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A contravention of this policy by a person to whom this policy applies may result in summary dismissal.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Breach of the notification, Closed Period or short-term trading rules through collar execution or unwind carries employment consequences beyond the transaction itself.

summary: A funded collar is likely possible for Key Management Personnel under this policy, because it is silent on margin lending, secured financing and encumbrance, so no express prohibition blocks the loan leg. The put and call, being derivative financial products issued over the Company's shares (and, in any event, caught by the broad dealing and hedging provisions), require prior notification to the Chairman (directors) or Managing Director (other KMP), or the Company Secretary if either of those officers is the one dealing, with an indication that there is no impediment, and must be executed outside the recurring Closed Periods around annual, half-year and quarterly results and outside any Board-imposed ad hoc prohibition. Structuring should keep the arrangement outside the 6-month short-term trading ban (which itself becomes a further Closed Period), since only a hardship waiver from the Review Officer can excuse early unwind or disposal within that window. Any dealing must be reported to the Company Secretary immediately, with details following within 2 business days, and directors' trades are separately notified to the ASX under Appendix 3Y. Because the policy does not address financing at all, banks should confirm independently that no unwritten board practice or side letter restricts pledging vested shares, as the absence of an express prohibition is not the same as an express permission.
